evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Joanna says 'in order for me to provide you a personalized estimate just need to ask you some questions about this might, might take about ten to fifteen minutes if this is a good time but we definitely have an availability for Tuesday' — time-boxed and availability confirmed, but no explicit wait for a yes before moving into discovery.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Asked late: 'Okay, so do you have any important concerns aside from the pricing? I'm gonna discuss it of course, or do you have any other concerns that you also want to discuss on this call?' This came after substantial logistics probing.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raised concern about 2 PM timing for key pickup. Joanna followed up: 'Is there a specific reason why that's gonna be our preferred start time? Is it access issues or whatnot?' Customer explained keys not available until 2 PM, needing to pick them up, then return. Joanna confirmed understanding: 'Mm-hmm so what's the earliest time we can start? Just to make sure.' and 'so what's the earliest time we can start? Probably like 3330 [3:30].' Clear two-layer follow-up.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: After clarifying the timing need, Joanna summarizes: 'Okay, alright. So, I'll just leave a note that the closer time that closer to the 3:00 PM arrival. But the guys will definitely give you a call once we're on the, they're on the way.' She reflects back what she heard and confirms the solution.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Property type (apartment), floor (second), stairs vs. elevator (stairs only), rooms (one bedroom), walking distance (immediate left from stairs), parking (spot available by stairs), special considerations (no large items except dresser, TV stand, table, two small end tables, coffee table, queen mattress/box spring), box count (standard size boxes, within typical range). All seven logistics items covered.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Asked explicitly: 'Alright, so in terms of you're good with packing. Everything's all packed good to go or do you need help with packing as well?' Customer declined.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Yes: 'And how about boxes? Are you also moving some boxes typically for one bedroom apartment? It's like $15 to 25 in total. Do you think you would just fall within that range?'
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Joanna provides both anchor and personalization: 'typically a one bedroom apartment usually takes two and a half to three and a half hours to complete for your move. I just quote you more on the twenty and a half to three hour mark. Which is an estimated budget of $480.76 to $576 this for a three hour job.' She personalizes to customer's items (no couch, no appliances, dresser/TV stand/tables/mattress only) and notes 'Especially it's, there's, you know, we might fall within the typical range of two and half to three and a half hours as well.'
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Joanna covers: hourly rate ($192/two men, $96 per mover), all-inclusive framing ('everything we need to complete your move is already in that price'), fee transparency (lists reps, insurance, assembly/reassembly, 'no hidden fees', 'no credit card fees', 'no sterle fees'), and 2.5-hour minimum with 15-minute increments: 'for any move this a two and a half hour minimum if we go over, we only charge in fifteen minute intervals.'
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Never asked. After quote presentation, customer immediately asks 'Okay, that's fine' and then later asks about deposit. Joanna never asks 'Does that feel fair?' or holds silence for customer reaction.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Fully delivered with discount terms: 'And lastly on time guarantee if we run late, we provide discounts for your move again, no hidden fees of any type.'
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Partial. Joanna mentions it: 'And we also include our no worries damage coverage which would give you up to $2,000 coverage for any repair replacement reimbursement for any accidental damages.' However, she does not frame it as 'no deductible/no fine print' or confirm it's built into the rate (not an add-on). She states it's included in pricing but does not use the specific no-deductible/no-fine-print language from the script.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No. After covering Two Promises section, Joanna moves directly to the explicit ask ('would you like our help for this move on Tuesday?') without asking a version of 'Does that put those to rest?' to confirm the promises answered the customer's concerns.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Not asked. Joanna moves from booking confirmation and rate-lock explanation directly into sending confirmation email. No genuine 'What's still concerning you?' or 'any questions?' check.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: No. Joanna does not ask a version of 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' before closing.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Full. Joanna asks plainly: 'Okay. Mm-hmm so, with that being said would you like our help for this move on Tuesday?' No built-in out, direct ask without softening.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: Yes. Joanna states 'we don't take deposit. The payment is only upon completion of the move' (payment is due at completion, not locked in advance, but rate is locked via the quote).
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Partial. Confirmed: date (Tuesday), preferred arrival window (3 PM after customer clarification), addresses (pickup 1535 west contour drive apt 22, dropoff 5622 Evers road), apartment type (both one-bedroom, second floor, stairs). Missing: explicit phone number re-confirmation (Joanna had it at the start but does not re-confirm it at booking), crew size (not stated — 'two men' was implied in pricing but not explicitly confirmed as the crew count for this move), and notes about customer's concern (Joanna did leave a note about timing preference '3:00 PM arrival' but did not summarize her understanding of the key-pickup issue or any other customer worry beyond the time window).

top_strength: Joanna gathered thorough logistics details and genuinely dug into the customer's primary concern about timing, uncovering the root cause (key unavailability at 2 PM) and confirming the solution, which is exactly what two-layers-deep discovery should look like.
coaching_note: Add a genuine final concerns check ('What's still concerning you about this move?' not 'any questions?') before the explicit ask, and hold silence after quoting ('Does that feel fair?') to let the customer react naturally — both are high-leverage pauses that Joanna skipped.
